chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'mam ibn al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Eight [types of slave-women] are not permissible for your marriage: your slave-woman and her mother; your slave-woman and her sister; your slave-woman and she is your aunt (paternal) through breastfeeding; your slave-woman and she is your aunt (maternal) through breastfeeding; your slave-woman and she breastfed you; your slave-woman and she has been impregnated [by another] until she completes her waiting period with one menstruation; your slave-woman and she is pregnant by another; your slave-woman and she is in her dower period; your slave-woman and she has a husband.' And whenever a man marries a young slave-girl and his wife breastfeeds her, both become prohibited to him. That which indicates this is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What are the eight types of slave-women prohibited for marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (AS) details eight prohibitions on marrying one's own slave-women, blending blood, marriage, and breastfeeding (radāʿ) kinship with specific physical states like pregnancy or menstruation. It highlights the juristic principle that a master's wife breastfeeding a slave-girl creates a permanent bond, prohibiting the master from marrying her, thereby extending the scope of radāʿ beyond direct maternal nursing. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic marriage laws regarding slaves while maintaining strict ethical and biological boundaries.
